content:
Percentage makes its debut in Class 5 — conversions, percent-of, and increase/decrease. It's the bridge to profit-loss and data questions, and Olympiad papers lean on it. Here is what the chapter tests, with a free 10-question test.

What the Class 5 Maths Olympiad Percentage chapter tests

  • Percent ↔ fraction ↔ decimal conversions
  • Percentage of a quantity
  • What percent one number is of another
  • Percentage increase and decrease

Key facts your child should know

  • Per cent means per hundred: 45% = 45/100 = 0.45.
  • x% of N = (x/100) × N — 30% of 250 = 75.
  • "What % is a of b" = (a ÷ b) × 100.
  • 25% = 1/4, 50% = 1/2, 75% = 3/4, 20% = 1/5.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Dividing by the wrong number in "what percent" questions.
  • Adding percentage points instead of computing on the original.
  • Forgetting the whole is always 100%.

quiz.title: IMO Class 5 Percentage Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten Olympiad-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: Which fraction in lowest terms equals 16%?
questions.explanation: 16% = 16/100; dividing top and bottom by 4 gives 4/25.

questions.q: In a classroom activity, 54 tiles on a 100-tile floor are blue. What percentage does this represent?
questions.explanation: Percent means "per hundred". 54 out of 100 is exactly 54%.

questions.q: There are 21 houses with solar panels in a colony of 50. What percentage is this?
questions.explanation: Scale to 100: 21 out of 50 = 42 out of 100 = 42%.

questions.q: What decimal number is equal to 9%?
Out of 40 children in a dance club, 22 are girls. What percent are they?
A school has 840 students and 55% of them come by bus. How many students come by bus?
Express the fraction 3/4 as a percentage.
Express the fraction 7/20 as a percentage.

faq.q: How do you find 30% of a number?
faq.a: Multiply by 30 and divide by 100 — or find 10% and triple it. 30% of 250 = 75.
